open.thesis: Do not sell Terry McLaurin. open.thesis: New comparison, created because chem-hold-coker-benched closed on its own converse clause: Coker went FULL on Friday and is off Carolina's injury report entirely, so he is a live flex option rather than a frozen seat. Hold McLaurin in the RB/WR flex anyway. The two are half a point apart on projection (12.5 to 12.0) and STRATEGY section 10 forbids proposing a move worth under a point, so the tiebreakers decide. ROUTE SHARE: McLaurin 92.1% in Week 1, highest on Washington; Coker 71%. TARGET SHARE: Coker 24.3% on 9 targets to McLaurin's 4, which is the half that favours Coker and is not dismissed. GAME ENVIRONMENT, which is the decider: Washington at Dallas is a 50.5-point game, the highest total on the entire Week 2 board, with Washington implied 23.25 and Dallas playing single-high on 54.5% of snaps; Carolina at Atlanta is 43.5 with Carolina 2.5-point FAVOURITES against a Cooper Rush offence, which is a leading-and-running script that suppresses pass volume. Coker's Week 1 line was 138 yards and two touchdowns - STRATEGY section 2 says target share and route participation are the floor and touchdown rate is the noise, and two touchdowns is the noisiest part of the best receiving line either man has. || REVIEWED 19 Sep 04:40Z (Friday 22:40 Mexico City): HELD, and strengthened by something new. Coker rolled his left ankle in the first quarter of Week 1 and was in a walking boot Monday - background this run picked up for the first time via Pro Football Network, written after Wednesday's practice, where he was limited and Dave Canales said 'I expect him to play on Sunday'. TIMESTAMP DISCIPLINE: yesterday's 22:10Z run had LATER information - full Friday participation and removal from the report entirely - so the ankle is history, not current status, and it does NOT strengthen the hold the way it first appeared to. Against that, DraftKings Network call him a strong start on a 26.5% target share that led Carolina, ahead of Tetairoa McMillan's eight targets, with 102 air yards - so the clause about Carolina naming him the primary target is closer to firing than it was. Held on game environment: Washington implied 23.5 in a 50.5-point game against Carolina 23.0 in a 44.5-point game, plus McLaurin's 92.1% Week 1 route share and DraftKings' own warning that two touchdowns on nine targets is not repeatable. This is the closest call in the Chem brief.

Or Washington place McLaurin on the Saturday report. Or Carolina name Coker the primary target ahead of Tetairoa McMillan in any Saturday reporting, which would make the 24.3% a floor rather than a ceiling.

open.thesis: Recorded as a DECLINE so a future run does not rediscover this brief's own three-day recommendation and re-issue it. The vacancy behind him is real - A.J. Brown is on injured reserve for six games, Hollins slid into the role the moment Brown left, took 18 of the first 32 snaps and led New England in receiving with 4 catches for 51 yards. Pitts cannot enter Chem's RB/WR flex in any week this season and is behind Cooper Rush, Atlanta's third-string quarterback, confirmed today with Penix ruled out and Tua out; Atlanta are implied 21.5. Andrews took 25% of Baltimore's targets in Week 1 - tied with Zay Flowers for the team lead - Flowers is DOUBTFUL with a hamstring, and Baltimore carry a 27.75 implied total, the highest of any team any AVIATO player is on, against a New Orleans defence implied 19.25 that allowed 206 receiving yards, two scores and seven red-zone targets in Week 1. Projections are 10.4 against 10.4, so STRATEGY's floor on lowering projected points is untouched. Pitts's is the only seat on this roster outside the seven-day churn window. STATED COST: Pitts at 93.4% rostered is the roster's only real trade chip and this spends it; no Chem team has lost its starting tight end, so there is no buyer this week. SOURCE DISCARDED, recorded because it nearly went in: a Sports Illustrated Week 2 must-sit list naming Andrews describes Baltimore facing Cleveland and calls Isaiah Likely inactive - Likely has been a Giant all season and Baltimore play New Orleans. He is the top why=OWNED running back on the Chem wire at 66.4% rostered, which is the band STRATEGY section 4 calls the strongest single wire signal, and he was researched tonight for the first time. closed.summary: One bench slot went Goedert -> Allgeier -> Likely in five days. Each step was defensible on projection; the sequence gained nothing and cost two roster moves.
Recommended dropping Kyle Monangai for Tre Tucker on 13 Sep. Monangai returned from the knee and scored 20.4; Tucker's Bowers-vacuum thesis now has a return date on it. Not acted on.

A 13 Sep run recommended adding Xavier Worthy and dropping Isaiah Likely, on the reasoning that a second TE is structurally unplayable in a RB/WR flex. Likely then scored 27.8 with two touchdowns. The structural argument was sound and the conclusion was still wrong, because it valued the slot rather than the player.

The 22:09Z 14 Sep run published Chem reporting a FINAL score of 152.9-90.4. Neither was true: 152.9 added benched Isaiah Likely's 27.8 to the starting total of 125.1, and Nicky Jam still had Kenneth Walker III and the Chiefs D/ST to play on Monday night. It also shipped an empty trades array over a live proposal. Both corrected at 16:40.

Adding Isaiah Likely on 13 Sep resolved RIGHT - 27.8 with two touchdowns. Note for the pattern file: the add landed at 19:03Z, two hours after Pitts's 17:00Z kickoff, so he could never have been started in week 1. The cost of a Sunday-evening add is a whole week, not a lineup slot.

The hold-the-Jaguars-D/ST thesis is retired after one week, reversed by its own logic rather than against it. It held Jacksonville because Week 2 rankings had them 4th and Baltimore 5th. Lindy's Week 2 board now has Baltimore 2nd hosting New Orleans and Jacksonville 9th travelling to Denver. Same method, moved input, opposite answer - and the Week 1 result the hold produced was 12.0 with five sacks, so the original call was right for the week it covered. If Jacksonville finish top 5 at Denver anyway, reopen this as CHURN.

The 14 Sep worthALook row led with 'Chris Rodriguez Jr. owns the Jacksonville goal line.' Sports Illustrated's Week 1 backfield review has him at 41% of snaps, six touches and 'relegated to short-yardage duty', with one red-zone carry - the only one any Jacksonville back got. He was moved to doNotChase this run with the correction stated in whatWentWrong. The lesson is that 'owns the goal line' is a claim that needs a red-zone carry count behind it, not a role description. VINDICATED IN SUBSTANCE 16 Sep 05:55Z: Draft Sharks' Week 1 usage review states Rodriguez 'took the only goal-line snap and five of the team's eight short-yardage plays' and ran two MORE pass routes than Tuten. So the original claim was directionally right and only the evidence behind it was missing - the correction was about rigour, not about the fact.

The McLaurin + Stafford for DeVonta Smith offer is withdrawn from the action list after three runs unanswered, on reporting rather than on age. Its own falsification clause named 'McLaurin's role recovers, which would make selling him at his lowest point the mistake'; Draft Sharks' Week 1 review has him at 92.1% route participation, highest on Washington, against Diggs at 65.8%, with Mitchell and Woolen covering him on 22 of 35 routes for one target. Coordinator David Blough has said the offense is built around getting him ten targets a game, and Dallas are missing safety Malik Hooker. Four targets was coverage, not decline, and the strategy file's rule is to buy usage and sell efficiency. The offer stays published in the trades section with the reasoning attached - it recomputes to +21.8/+3.8 unchanged - but it is no longer recommended and should not be re-sent. Stafford being dead weight is still true; there is no one-for-one on either roster where both sides gain, so McLaurin was the only thing making it clear, and that is the problem. RE-PRICED 16 Sep 05:55Z: still +21.8/+3.8 on season projections, unchanged for a fifth snapshot - but priced on THIS WEEK's projections the other side comes out at minus 0.1, so it does not clear the both-sides-gain test at all. The entire +3.8 lives in a frozen preseason field. Recorded because it changes how the offer should be read, not whether it is sent.

The hold on Chris Boswell was argued from the other league's transaction log. It said 'Pineiro was dropped FOR Boswell on 8 September, six days ago' and invoked the two CHURN entries - but the 8 Sep Boswell add and the pair of CHURN entries are both IPADE's Little-Boswell reversal. chem-claim-ravens-dst-2026-09-15 is closed as superseded, not reversed. Its argument - drop the Jacksonville defense, which FantasyPros has 30th on the explicit reasoning that its five Week 1 sacks came against Cleveland and will not repeat at Denver - is unchanged and still drives the replacement card. What was wrong was the name. Tampa Bay is 1st on that same FantasyPros board, 1st on FantasyLife's 15 Sep streamer column at 3% rostered nationally, and 4th on Sportsnaut's against Baltimore's 6th: every board retrieved this run puts Tampa above Baltimore. Tampa also draws Cleveland this week, so it inherits the exact fixture that built Jacksonville's reputation, and at 13.1% rostered here against Baltimore's 89.8% it is far less likely to be taken by one of the four managers above AVIATO in priority. This is an omission being corrected - Tampa Bay sat on the wire unnamed through three consecutive readings of this seat - rather than a thesis flipping, and it should not be logged as CHURN. Baltimore is retained as the explicit fallback in worthALook.

The 04:30 brief asserted that nothing on Jalen Coker's ankle had been published since 14 September and accepted a blind claim on that basis. The premise was false. DraftKings Network's Week 2 injury round-up, dated 15 September, carries Coker under Ankle as 'Expected to play Sunday', quotes him calling the injury minor, and notes he led Carolina in receiving in Week 1 - one day newer than the sources already cited on the card, and from a publisher the card already used. The conclusion was unaffected (the claim was first in the queue either way) so this cost nothing, but the failure mode is worth the entry: the run searched the player's name and never searched the week's aggregated injury report. GENERALISABLE LESSON: search the week's aggregated injury report as a matter of course, not only the individual player. Also logged: a CBS Sports item titled 'Panthers' Jalen Coker: Logs full practice' ranks at the top of search for this player and is dated 8 October 2025, describing a quadriceps injury from a different season. It is the highest-ranked trap on this name and was correctly excluded this run.

PROCESS ERROR, caught and corrected within fifteen minutes. This run's first publish of both daily files was validated against the validator EMBEDDED IN RUNBOOK.md rather than against validate.py in the repo. VALIDATORS.md states plainly that the repo copy is the only gate and that the inline runbook duplicate has drifted - and it has: the runbook copy assumes youGive/youGet are bare ID lists, so it crashes outright on the live nine-section schema, and it lacks the roster-state, grade-vocabulary, case-block and cannotSee rules the real one enforces. Run against the real validator, both published files FAILED twice: roster.state was 'PRE-KICKOFF' where the legal values are THURSDAY/SUNDAY/FINAL, and unresearched matchups used a grade of 'NOT_RESEARCHED' where the correct mechanism is omitting grade and setting notResearched: true. Both were fixed and republished, and both now exit 0 against repo validate.py. The previously published files DID pass the real gate, so this run briefly regressed them. LESSON FOR FUTURE RUNS: fetch and run validate.py from the repository BEFORE publishing; do not trust the runbook's inline copy, and do not trust the runbook's claim to be 'everything you need' - STRATEGY.md and VALIDATORS.md exist alongside it and both change the answer.

Claim landed 07:14: Jalen Coker in, Matthew Stafford out. The blind-claim risk resolved well - Draft Sharks 14 Sep have Coker calling it a rolled ankle from the first quarter against Chicago, boot precautionary, expects to play at Atlanta, averaging 16.0 PPR over his last eight. Continues as chem-hold-coker-2026-09-16.

Lost, not wrong. Footballers claimed the Buccaneers D/ST at 07:14 from one place higher in priority (9th to AVIATO's 10th) and dropped New England to do it. The queue fell through to Baltimore, 3rd of 32 on FantasyPros' Week 2 board against a New Orleans offence ranked 26th. The argument for dropping Jacksonville was correct; the queue position was the whole story. First time the invisible-rival-claims limitation has cost a named card, and it should be cited the next time a card is ordered.

Claim landed 07:14: Tyler Loop in, Chris Boswell out. Pro Football Network's Week 2 kicker board has Loop K4 and Boswell K17 - a wider gap than when the card was written. Continues as chem-hold-loop-2026-09-16.

PROCESS ERROR REPEATED, and it is the second time. The closed entry dated 16 Sep 06:10 already records this exact failure and ends 'LESSON FOR FUTURE RUNS: fetch and run validate.py from the repository BEFORE publishing; do not trust the runbook's inline copy'. This run read RUNBOOK.md end to end, including its KNOWN LIMITATIONS, ran the validator embedded in it, got exit 0 on both files, and published. Only afterwards did a listing of the repository root reveal validate.py, VALIDATORS.md, STRATEGY.md and the two decisions-*.json files - none of which RUNBOOK.md mentions while describing itself as 'everything you need'. Consequence: the first IPADE publish at 13:28Z carried youGive and youGet as flat integer arrays, because that is what the runbook's Step 6 schema and its inline validator require. The repository validator requires objects with playerId, name and detail, which is also the shape the app renders, so that publish would have shown the trade player chips as holes. Caught within four minutes, converted to objects, re-validated against repo validate.py (exit 0 on both files) and republished. THE LESSON HAS NOW FAILED TWICE BECAUSE IT LIVES ONLY IN THIS LOG, which a run has no reason to open until after it has published. The fix is not another log entry: delete the inline validator from RUNBOOK.md, and add STRATEGY.md, VALIDATORS.md, validate.py and decisions-*.json to the runbook's Step 1. A warning stored downstream of the mistake cannot prevent it.

REVERSED at the 16:00 CDMX run, nine hours after it was re-affirmed. The hold rested on two planks and both were re-examined. Plank one, that the section-9 structural argument 'burned once' when a 13 Sep run used it to recommend dropping Isaiah Likely: that is a real precedent but it is not this case. The Likely error was dropping the tight end who OCCUPIES the only TE slot; this is dropping the one who cannot reach it. The argument is the same sentence applied to opposite players, and treating the precedent as barring the sentence outright is what kept a dead roster seat alive for three runs. Plank two, that Pitts is Likely insurance: half right, and the new brief says so on the record. Mark Andrews is a FREE AGENT in Chem at 82.0% rostered, with Hockenson 62.7%, Juwan Johnson 53.5% and Hunter Henry 51.9% behind him - no claim, no waiting period - so insurance is abundant and free. The genuine residual exposure, now written into the brief's cannotSee, is that Andrews plays Sunday 11:00 and Likely plays Monday 18:15, so a Monday-morning ruling on Likely leaves only Terrance Ferguson at 6.0 projected. That is about a five-point downside on a narrow branch, traded for a flex-eligible receiver who can actually score in every other branch. Pitts's seat is also the only one on the roster outside the seven-day churn window - Coker, the Ravens D/ST and Tyler Loop all changed hands at 07:14 today. Replaced by chem-add-hollins-2026-09-16-pm.

THE COMPLAINT WAS WRONG AND IT WAS FILED TWICE. Two consecutive briefs recorded as a permanent structural defect that a 07:00 Mexico City task lands at 13:00 UTC, six hours after Chem settles claims at 07:00 UTC, and concluded that no brief can ever reach a waiver run. True of the MORNING run only. A second task fires at 16:00 Mexico City, which is 22:00 UTC, and this run generated at 22:15 UTC against claims clearing 07:00 UTC Thursday - a gap of eight hours forty-five minutes on the correct side, confirmed from the clearsAt field on every waiver row in the live snapshot rather than from memory. The afternoon run IS the waiver run. Recording this as WRONG rather than RESOLVED because the error was analytical, not circumstantial: nothing changed, the earlier runs simply did not check what else was scheduled. Lesson: before filing a scheduling defect, establish which runs exist. The separate observation in that entry - that settings.waiver.process lists every day except Tuesday, so there is a claim window nearly every night rather than one - is retained and remains true.

DECLINING DOUBS WAS RIGHT AND THE REASON GIVEN WAS WRONG. The entry declined him on 'three-way argument between Doubs, Hollins and Douglas' plus the section-3 projection floor. FantasyPros' Week 2 waiver column settles it: Doubs's Week 1 was zero catches on three targets with an interception charged against him, and the column names MACK HOLLINS as the player whose role was elevated by the A.J. Brown injury - four targets drawn after Brown went down, with red-zone access. So the A.J. Brown hole was real, and two consecutive runs pointed at the wrong beneficiary. The entry's own falsifiedIf clause anticipated this exactly - 'Mack Hollins is also free at 3.0% rostered and was NOT researched - check his number before assuming Doubs is the cheaper route to the same role' - and that check is what this run ran. Closed with Doubs retained on the candidates list purely so a future run does not rediscover a 59.8%-rostered name and treat it as new.

Stefon Diggs fallback retired: Bok-aneers claimed Diggs at 07:14 on 16 Sep, so the fallback target no longer exists. Brian Thomas Jr. was never ruled out, so the condition that would have reopened it never fired.

Falsification condition fired as written. Carolina's Wednesday report lists Jalen Coker LIMITED with the ankle after a walking boot earlier in the week; RotoWire describe him working on the side. The hold thesis said it was falsified if he was limited or DNP on the Wednesday or Thursday report. He stays on the roster - the churn rule closes a seat claimed 16 Sep, and he is already benched - but the thesis itself is closed rather than defended.

Closed on its own falsification clause, by a route the clause did not anticipate. The clause read 'beat reporting this week names DeMario Douglas or Romeo Doubs rather than Hollins as the man absorbing Brown's targets, which changes the incoming player without changing the outgoing one.' What actually happened is that a BETTER incoming player appeared on a different team's injury report: Baltimore list Zay Flowers DOUBTFUL and BaltimoreRavens.com state that if Flowers sits, 'Rashod Bateman would move into the top receiver spot'. Bateman projects 10.3 / 122.7 at 11.3% rostered against Hollins's 8.9 / 96.0 at 6.7%, in a 27.75-point offence against a 23.25-point one. Separately, the Yahoo beat writer this card relied on votes DeMario Douglas by volume (7 targets to Hollins's 4), which in full PPR is the deciding shape. The outgoing half - drop Pitts - was right for three runs and carries forward unchanged into chem-drop-pitts-add-bateman-2026-09-18-pm. Logged WRONG on the incoming name, not on the seat.

Resolved by its own converse clause: 'full participation Friday with no designation reinstates the original claim thesis unchanged.' Carolina's Friday practice report has Jalen Coker FULL and removed from the injury report entirely, after two limited sessions. Dave Canales did exactly what he said on Wednesday he would do. Coker's Week 1 was 8 catches on 9 targets for 138 and two touchdowns - a 24.3% target share on 71% route participation, described as a high-volume WR3 with weekly WR2 upside. He is a live flex candidate again rather than a dead seat, which is a different question from the one this thesis was answering, so it closes and chem-flex-mclaurin-over-coker-2026-09-18-pm opens in its place.

Resolved. Minnesota ruled Kyler Murray OUT with the concussion on Friday 18 September and named Carson Wentz the starter at Chicago - the outcome this thesis was recorded to protect against being misread. Sports Illustrated's fallout piece keeps Jefferson a must-start at WR6 on a 41% receiving-yard share, and Chicago's defence ranks 26th overall. The two sources that disagreed on Wednesday (SI's list printing Murray, Athlon reporting Wentz) no longer disagree. Nothing about Jefferson was ever in doubt; the thesis existed so a future run would not treat a backup quarterback as a sell signal, and it did its job.

Closed on the failure of its own act-condition: 'Murray clears the five-stage protocol and Addison draws seven or more targets in Week 2, or Jefferson misses time.' Murray did not clear - he was ruled OUT on Friday. Sports Illustrated's Wentz fallout column moves T.J. Hockenson from TE23 to TE14 and leaves Addison unchanged at WR60, with the reason stated flatly: 'Wentz cannot support two viable wide receivers.' Declined across five consecutive runs and closed rather than carried a sixth time. Only Jefferson missing time reopens it, and that is a different thesis.

The window this was about has shut. Woody Marks's waiver period closed at 07:00Z on Friday 18 September and this brief declined the claim; he is a free agent in Chem from 22 September in any case, so the cost question the thesis was built around no longer exists. Closed honestly rather than carried: I did not search Houston on the 18 Sep 22:10Z run, so I have nothing new on whether he is the lead back, and I removed his watch-list row rather than reprint an unchecked finding for a fourth time. If Houston name him the lead back he is a free add on Tuesday with no priority involved.

DraftKings Network published his Week 1 usage: 4.2% target share, last among ten Baltimore receivers, one target, zero catches, zero air yards, behind Chris Moore and LaJohntay Wester.
